ground_truth.mechanism: cart/src/services/CartService.cs EmptyCart (lines 74-100 at tag 3.0.0): with the flag at 100% (value 1), Random.Shared.NextDouble() < 1 is always true, so every EmptyCart call goes to _badCartStore, a second ValkeyCartStore built with the address badhost:1234 (cart/src/Program.cs:57-62) and never initialized. Its EmptyCartAsync calls EnsureRedisConnected (cartstore/ValkeyCartStore.cs:177-193, 74-124), which tries ConnectionMultiplexer.Connect inside a lock and, finding no connection, throws ApplicationException Wasn't able to connect to redis (line 98); EmptyCartAsync wraps it as RpcException FailedPrecondition Can't access cart storage. (line 191), and CartService records an exception event and ERROR status on the cart server span (lines 92-97). AddItem and GetCart use the working store and are unaffected. checkout calls EmptyCart from PlaceOrder after shipping and discards the error (checkout/main.go:373 `_ = cs.emptyUserCart(ctx, req.UserId)`, wrapper at 527-532), so checkout's oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart client span is ERROR FAILED_PRECONDITION while PlaceOrder returns OK. The error is swallowed, not the delay: one live trace on 2026-09-10 had the cart EmptyCart span at 212 s and PlaceOrder at 228 s, with frontend-proxy failing POST /api/checkout at its 15 s upstream timeout; those are cascading symptoms.

mechanism_truth: One operation of the service, emptying a user's cart, cannot connect to the data store it uses, while the same service's other storage operations keep working; every such request waits on the connection attempt and then fails with an error saying the storage cannot be reached. The calling service ignores that error and reports the order as placed, so the failure is silent at the caller, and any slowness or timeouts seen further up are only a consequence. Describing the wait as a hang or a timeout is also correct. An answer that says the data store is down for every operation, or that puts the fault in the caller or in the slow upstream requests, does not describe this mechanism.
notes: Version 1 draft, written 2026-10-28 from the 3.0.0 source (tag 3.0.0, commit 1755859a) and one live trace from the 2026-09-10 signal inventory; not yet run on this fixture, and both evidence files are still to be captured, so readiness fails until they exist. Source facts: the flag's variants are 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%, 100% and off (src/flagd/demo.flagd.json:31-44); only 100% is claimed here, because it makes every EmptyCart call fail. The load generator never calls EmptyCart (no match in src/load-generator/script.js at 3.0.0; its checkout tasks use a fresh user id each time, weight 2 of 29), so the fault is reached only through checkout's PlaceOrder after a successful charge and shipment. The bad store's connection is never registered with the Redis instrumentation (Program.cs:98-99 registers only the working store), so there is no client span to the bad address. Live trace of 2026-09-10 (taken by hand before the collector stripped flag telemetry, so it is not usable as evidence here): cart server span POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart, grpc.status_code 9, ERROR, status description Status(StatusCode="FailedPrecondition", Detail="Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis" followed by a .NET stack trace through ValkeyCartStore.cs lines 98 and 182, plus an exception event; checkout client span oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart, FAILED_PRECONDITION, ERROR; PlaceOrder OK; the string badhost:1234 appears nowhere in the span. signal_regex avoids the apostrophe in Wasn't so it matches whether a renderer escapes it or not. Baseline: EmptyCart already had 3 ERROR calls in 138 in span metrics on 2026-09-10 with the message unknown, so baseline_absence must be captured with the regex, not with error status. Locus: cart, because the flag evaluation, the failing store call and the first ERROR span are all in cart and cart's server span exists (unlike paymentUnreachable); valkey-cart is healthy and keeps serving AddItem and GetCart. Operation: the cart server span name as seen live on 2026-09-10, plus the checkout client span name and the bare RPC name. cascade_rule names checkout because it is the direct caller that hides the error; frontend-proxy's 504s on POST /api/checkout also occur at baseline. Timing, inferred from source and the single live trace, not measured on this fixture: the connect attempt runs inside a lock on the one bad store instance (ValkeyCartStore.cs:82-91) and _isRedisConnectionOpened stays false, so concurrent EmptyCart calls queue behind each other at roughly one per connect attempt (212 s in the one sample). Spans export only when they end, so the first signal trace may appear minutes after the flip and three need several attempts; signal_wait_s 1200 is a judgment for that, not a measurement. The queue and the multiplexers it creates (each failed Connect leaves a ConnectionMultiplexer that is never disposed) live in the cart process and are not cleared by restoring the flag, which is why restart_before_run restarts cart; restart cart again before a batch of any other scenario. Whether that growth or checkout's waiting goroutines push cart (160M limit) or checkout (64M in the overlay) into an OOM restart is unknown; expected_restarts is left empty on purpose so such a restart makes a trial INVALID until a soak shows otherwise. deterministic yes: every EmptyCart call under the flag fails; only the latency grows with time since the flip. Evidence captured 2026-10-28 on Jaeger main-238c5fa2: flag set to 100% at 07:41:02Z (OFREP confirmed value 1); the signal appeared in 1 cart trace 149 s after the flip (fa20327c7325d6718c894b30428788f3, saved from GET /api/v3/traces/{id}); bench.py oracle PASS at call 2 (get_trace_errors); fixture_leak --live PASS under the fault (192 traces, all services; 51 cart and checkout). Baseline: 200 cart traces 07:33:37Z to 07:40:37Z with the flag off, no match. signal_wait_s stays 1200 as an upper bound; one measurement is not a distribution.
